full_judgment: 4. The plaintiff’s case, in short, was that the suit property originally belonged to Surendra Chandra Chowdhury who died leaving son Samir Kumar Chowdhury. That Samir Kumar Chowdhury got the suit property as heir of Surendra Chandra Chowdhury and-also as legatee of a will Samir Kumar Chowdhury entered into a contract with the plaintiff on. 30.09.1965 for sale of the suit property at a consideration of Tk. 17,000/-. That it was stipulated in the deed of contract that out of total consideration money Tk. 6,000/- would remain with the plaintiff on account of expenses for arranging a valid employment voucher in the United Kingdom for Samir Kumar Chowdhury and passport, air ticket etc. and that the plaintiff would procure all those within five months from the date of execution of the deed of contract and that the remaining 11,000/- taka would be paid at the time of execution of sale deed after taking necessary income tax clearance etc. That on the date of that agreement possession of the properly was delivered to the plaintiff. That in the meantime the Sub-Divisional Officer, Habigonj issued a notice for acquisition of the suit property under the defence of Pakistan Rules and evicted the plaintiff and the opposite party No. 1 there from. Plaintiff and Samir Kumar Chowdhury then filed Writ Petition No. 99 of 1966 challenging the acquisition of the suit property and got rule which was subsequently made absolute on 09.02.1967. That Samir Kumar Chowdhury also filed Civil Revision No. 851 of 1966 in connection with grant of probate of the will which was ultimately disposed of in favour of Samir Kumar Chowdhury. That the plaintiff ultimately could not procure the employment voucher in U.K. for Samir Kumar Chowdhury as per contract. That Samir Kumar Chowdhury requested the plaintiff to adjust the expenses of the litigations from the said amount of Tk.6,000/- Plaintiff, accordingly, spent Tk. 1,734/- towards the expenses of the writ petition and the civil revision. That the plaintiff subsequently paid Tk. 11,000/- to Samir Kumar Chowdhury by executing a promissory note on 5th Agrahayan 1372 B.S. and the plaintiff was put into possession of a portion of the suit property. That it was agreed upon that the said amount would be adjusted towards the consideration money but, if for any reason the parties decided not to execute the kabala, then Samir Kumar Chowdhury would refund the said amount of Tk. 11,000/- to the plaintiff. That the plaintiff thereafter filed Money Suit No. 10 of 1968 as the limitation of the promissory note was expiring but that suit was dismissed on technical ground. That as the sale deed could not be executed within the stipulated time of five months, Samir Kumar Chowdhury executed a memorandum on 30.07.1966 to the effect that the period of five months as mentioned in the deed of contract would start from the date of disposal of the writ petition and the civil revision. That the defendants Syeda Sirajunnessa Khatun and her husband Abdur Rahman used to live near the suit property and they were aware of the contract between the plaintiff and Samir Kumar Chowdhury and that these two defendants influenced Samir Kumar Chowdhury to issue a notice upon the plaintiff on 15.01.1966 alleging some false and concocted allegations. Thereafter these defendants collusively procured permission from the Deputy Commissioner. Sylhet for sale of the suit property and obtained a sale deed from Samir Kumar Chowdhury in respect of the suit property.
